Is something as small as a 250 going to be too small? Either in engine size or frame size? If you don't think I can get away with a 250 or 300, would 450 or 500 be sufficient?

a light 450-500 might be good place.

A Suzuki DRZ400 would be a good bike to learn on. It's a little tall for me stock with me being 5' 10" and weigh 150lbs. I can hit 90 on mine with a very simple rejeting of the carburetor and cutting a hole in the air box.

I also had a Suzuki DR350 and it was an awesome bike till it got stolen while getting shipped half way across the country. Would be a good bike as well. Not as fast as the DRZ but very reliable, they can be had for pretty cheap if you do some searching/waiting.

The KLR650 is also a great bike as well. Plenty of parts out there to turn it into a great commuter and long distance rider.

Older 250 will probably not be big enough, but a fuel injected one such as the WR250R would be a great fit. Pretty good bike from everything I gathered, costs a bit more than the other options though.

All these bikes would be a pretty good fit to learn on, that should be tall enough for you to ride comfortably as they are tall to ride off road. They should be able to get you out of a situation if you need to lay on the throttle.
Honda NC700X might do you well. My commute is similar to yours and it works perfect for it. Plus I can drive like an asshole and still average above 55-60mpg.

The suggestions I've seen here are pretty good, two more I'll throw in:

Yamaha FZ-6. I think they made them from 2004 to 2009. They're pretty tall and I found them very comfortable for short and long rides. It was extraordinarily reliable.
